business_scope.primary_industry_name: Construction of Cable-Stayed Bridges and Heavy Highway Viaducts

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 17 December 1985)
France–China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 30 May 1984, amended by protocol of 2 February 2013)
EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (applicable to France as an EU Member State)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement between the EU and Canada (CETA) (provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L.561-1 et seq.; Law No. 2024-364 of 22 April 2024 implementing EU AML/CFT standards; Decree No. 2020-118 and application of Act No. 2016-1691 (Sapin II); Code de commerce Articles L.561-46 to L.561-49 and R.561-1 to R.561-14 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); AMF General Regulation Article 315-7; French Constitution and public order principles.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each individual beneficial owner / legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority of the country of origin (e.g., national police, immigration authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the issuer is party to the 1961 Hague Convention) or French Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate registry extract for any legal entity shareholder or ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent commercial registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address and actual physical business presence for the departing entity or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local municipal authority, utility provider, or registered agent as per the law of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or sworn translation into French; notarization required for land-register-derived documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of funds/wealth declaration for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin commercial bank duly supervised in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or cosignature by the credit institution's compliance officer and sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate / police clearance certificate for directors and managers (case judiciaire), where legally available
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization; sworn translation into French

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French, EU, OFAC, UN, and domestic financial sanctions lists before engagement; enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined in Arabian Monetary and Financial Code Article L.561-10-II and Directive (EU) 2015/849, including family members and close associates; systematic consultation of the French Tracfin data collection system for suspicious transaction reporting; annual independent AML/CFT audit and periodic re-screening of UBOs, directors, and counterparties on a risk-sensitive basis; integration with EU asset-freeze consolidated list and the OECD Global Forum transparency standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) and the Guichet Unique Électronique via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr operated by INPI, researching the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and the Registre National des Marques
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be written in Latin script and may contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, and standard punctuation; foreign alphabets must be transliterated into Latin characters; the name must not indicate any activity inconsistent with the registered corporate purpose of an SARL; a denomination that is composed solely of common descriptive terms without distinguishing elements will be rejected; where a registered trademark is used for identity, the exact orthography and transliteration must be verified for prior-art infringement under French IP law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection, the applicant shall first obtain the written refusal decision from the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or from the INPI service via the Guichet Unique. Within two months of notification, an assignation in summary proceedings must be filed with the relevant Tribunal Judiciaire (commercial division) requesting annulment of the refusal or re-examination of the dossier. The applicant may alternatively amend the proposed denomination and resubmit the formation file through the same Guichet Unique portal, attaching the previous refusal decision and proof of modification. If a trademark opposition is lodged, a pre-litigation letter to the INPI trademark division is recommended prior to initiating a nullity action before the Tribunal Judiciaire.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted only as a registered seat of the SARL under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, provided that the company uses an approved domiciliation provider (operator of a service with a physical office in France) and the company maintains the document repository legally required at that seat. For highway bridge construction and heavy viaduct EPC contracting, a virtual seat is strongly discouraged and will not suffice for obtaining the mandatory French construction equipment liability certificate, contractor’s licence (certificat de qualification SNEC/OPQTB), professional civil liability insurance, and the public-procurement eligibility certificate; a physical operational base and full accounting substance must be separately established in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% within the first 12 months of registration for a non-resident-owned construction and infrastructure contractor; mandatory on-site inspection upon first public-works award; recurrent risk of unannounced labour inspectorate, tax asset seizure, and social-security fraud inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence, UBO piercing, AML/CFT file preparation, and sanctions screening report for the SARL non-resident ownership chain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External French law firm / compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border pre-incorporation AML compliance, advised hours and expert certification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and/or French consular legalization of origin-country corporate and personal documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign apostille office and French consular section in the issuing country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Hague Convention fees plus statutory consular service charges; paid per bundle of required documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and negative certificate / prior trademark verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for recordal and search, fixed fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal formation announcement in an authorised journal d'annonces légales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per publication line for SARL formation notices under French Commercial Code.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique electronic filing and insertion of the SARL into the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI operating the Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registrar fee by statutory tariff for creation of a commercial company with share capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the beneficial owner declaration (RBE) with the Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce competent for the registered seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed administrative fee under Decree No. 2020-118 and regulation of the commercial court registrars.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the initial share capital deposit certificate, where the contribution is cash
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Bank depositing funds (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or participant financial institution) and the notary issuing the report on disposable funds
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Deposit certificate and blocked funds certificate tariff set by banking practice or notary's fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and notarization of the articles of association (statuts) for the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French notary or law firm with power of attorney procedure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chamber of Notaries tariff schedule or prevailing legal-market benchmark for drafting bilingual notarized incorporation bylaws.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement with approved French domiciliation provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company approved by the Préfecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual domiciliation price per commercial rental rate, plus option for meeting-room access and mail handling.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L.210-1 to L.210-13 and L.223-1 to L.223-43 for the SARL; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. for registration at the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprise managed by Infogreffe)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 / Déclaration unique de création d'entreprise (electronic filing through Guichet Unique)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Articles of Association may set the capital from €1 upward. The full share capital must be subscribed, and each share must be allocated by name. At least 20% of cash contributions must be effectively paid-up at incorporation unless full payment is stipulated in the Articles, with the balance paid within five years; cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank or notary account, released only upon RCS registration, while in-kind contributions are fully paid-up and verified by a commissaire aux apports where required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SHAREHOLDERS AND MANAGER OF FR_SARL, adopted on [Date] at [Place]. The shareholders unanimously resolve: 1. Subscription of Capital — approve the subscription and allocation of the issued share capital as set out in the Articles of Association; the statutory capital is fully subscribed and cash contributions are accepted. 2. Registered Office — adopt the registered office located at [Address] in [City], France; any transfer of the seat is legally authorised. 3. Officers — appoint [Full Name] as Manager (Gérant) for a renewable term with full corporate powers, and [Name] as statutory auditor if required. This resolution takes effect upon registration with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles and Deposit Paid-up Capital in Blocked Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French-licensed bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Association complying with Article L.223-1 et seq. Each cash contributor transfers its subscribed amount to a blocked account opened in the company's name, and obtains a certificate of deposit from the bank or notary. The Articles must state the corporate purpose covering construction of highway bridges and viaducts (ISIC 4210), name, form (SARL), registered office, share capital, allocation of shares, term (up to 99 years), and the Gérant's powers. Non-cash contributions must be valued by a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) unless all associates waive the valuation in permitted cases.
required_dossiers: Project of Articles of Association (statuts)
Identity documents of all associates and the Gérant
Certificate of deposit of paid-up cash contributions
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (if contributions in kind)
Declaration under Article L.223-3 of no legal incapacity and no convictions of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the credit institution refuses the blocked account, use another eligible bank or notary; if the in-kind valuation is contested, appoint a court-designated appraiser or file a rectification before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Mandatory Legal Announcement in an Authorized Legal Newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved by the Prefect of the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation legal notice through the JAL portal or the Guichet Unique. The notice must cover the company name, legal form, registered office, object, duration, share capital, amounts paid-in, and identity of the Gérant. Obtain the attestation (attestation de parution) and reserve a publication date that is not more than three months before the RCS application.
required_dossiers: Legal announcement questionnaire / mandate
Project or signed Articles of Association
Identity and address of the Gérant
Proposed registered-office address and supporting proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL refuses publication because of inconsistent details, correct the draft and submit to another approved JAL in the same department; if refused twice, seek a prefectural designation of a JAL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Package with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (entreprendre.service-public.fr) and, for registry functions, Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet Unique and complete the electronic M0 company-creation declaration. Upload the signed Articles, capital deposit certificate, legal-announcement attestation, identity documents, and manager declarations. Pay the applicable registration, publication, and court-registry fees. The English or French data must be consistent; if contracts are in English, a French translation of required excerpts should be appended for the registry.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association in final form
Certificate of deposit of funds
Attestation of publication in an authorized legal newspaper
Electronic M0 / Guichet Unique declaration form
Power of attorney for the incorporator if the manager signs through an agent
Receipt of payment of registry and formalities fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or the registry issues a query, correct and resubmit within the statutory 15-day period. A refusal of inscription can be challenged before the judge responsible for registry supervision (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) or the Tribunal de Commerce in summary proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration in the RCS and Extract Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce competent for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: When the dossier is accepted, the registry records the company in the RCS and issues the official Extract Kbis (extrait Kbis), the unique corporate identity document. Verify the registered number, Articles, capital, manager, and corporate object. The Kbis constitutes proof of legal existence and authorises the opening of final bank accounts, contracting, and tax registrations.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract application generated through Infogreffe
Electronic filing receipt
Copy of the Articles as processed by the registry
Proof of company address and manager identity as recorded
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed beyond the statutory period, file a formal complaint with the registry supervisor; if the extract contains identity, capital, or manager errors, apply for judicial rectification at the presiding judge of the Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Statistical Registration (SIREN, SIRET, VAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFIP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) of the registered office; INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS registration normally triggers automatic assignment of SIREN and SIRET but should be verified at INSEE and the SIE. Apply for a French intra-community VAT number (FR + 2-digit key + SIREN) via the DGFIP/European portal if intra-Community supplies or invoicing are expected. If employees will be hired, register as an employer with URSSAF. Open operational bank account and retain the Kbis.
required_dossiers: Extract Kbis (or certificate of registration)
SIREN / SIRET notice or INSEE notice of identification
Proof of physical registered-office occupation (title or lease)
List of managers and beneficial owners for tax purposes
Company bank account details (IBAN) if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not issued or is incorrect, send a written request to the local SIE and the DGFIP National VAT Unit (BVNP); if a refusal is received, initiate the French amicable tax procedure under Articles L.1 to L.59 of the Book of Tax Procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), under the Ministry of Ecological Transition; coordinated with the Préfet of the project department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation Environnementale Unique (AE) for highway bridge construction and operation, accompanied by the construction authorisation under the French Urban Planning Code and the Police de l'eau / IOTA declaration or authorisation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecological Transition / Autorité Environnementale (MRAe) instructed by DREAL, with final decision by the Prefect
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Mandatory Full EIA Report for bridge or viaduct works comprised in a linear road project with developed length ≥ 100 m or total paved / impermeable surface ≥ 1 ha; otherwise preliminary case-by-case review (examen au cas par cas) under the Annex to Articles R.122-2 and R.181-1 of the Code de l'environnement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharge of treated construction water into natural receiving waters must respect pH 5.5–9.5, TSS ≤ 30 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 120 mg/L, and no visible hydrocarbon film. VOC emissions from asphalt plants and heat-treatment processes must not exceed 20 mg C/Nm³ at reference conditions. Hazardous waste is subject to declaration through the ADEME Vect'IA system; any water abstraction, impermeabilization, or works crossing a watercourse requires prior IOTA compliance with the Police de l'eau standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Construction site clearance requires: (i) fire safety certification from SDIS for site offices and worker accommodation; (ii) structural-load inspection certificate issued by a licensed bureau de contrôle for temporary works, falsework, and lifting plans; (iii) worker occupational-health validation under the Code du travail, including the Plan Particulier de Sécurité et de Protection de la Santé (PPSPS) approved by the SPS coordinator; and (iv) inspection certificates for cranes and lifting equipment under Decree No. 2009-483 and electrical conformity for temporary installations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French tax administration; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration via Guichet Unique: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a French SARL must file a single incorporation application through the Guichet Unique with certified articles of association, proof of legal existence from home country, and due-diligence KYC documentation. Upon completion, INSEE assigns the SIREN (enterprise identifier), the company is registered with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), and the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) allocates the definitive French tax ID (tax identification number) and, where applicable, an intra-community VAT number (FRxxxxxxxxx). Foreign companies without French establishment undertaking taxable supplies in France must submit a Form 10870 to the SIE to obtain a French VAT identification number before commencing taxable operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level. Statutory options include: (1) election for income tax as a pass-through under CGI article 239bis AA (family SARL) or article 239bis AB (young small SARL), subject to strict turnover and shareholder conditions; (2) option for French group tax consolidation under CGI article 223A for corporate groups; (3) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under CGI article 256C(2) for closely linked French entities. France does not maintain a 'check-the-box' regime; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD are statutorily binding.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French-established small businesses, the VAT franchise (small business exemption) applies up to EUR 85,000 annual turnover for goods and EUR 37,500 for services (2024/2025 statutory thresholds). Foreign-established entities supplying goods or services in France have no de minimis threshold and are required to register for French VAT immediately upon commencing any taxable supply, subject to the EU EUR 10,000 cross-border distance-selling threshold for final consumers if not otherwise subject to tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for domestic French B2B transactions will apply from 1 September 2026 (large and mid-size entities) and 1 September 2027 (small enterprises), through certified dematerialisation platforms (PDP) interoperating with the Public Invoice Portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF). E-invoicing requires a structured XML (Factur-X) or EDI format, real-time state of clearance/validation for accounting purposes, and XML mapping through exposed APIs. Export and B2C transactions are subject to mandatory e-reporting to the tax administration using the same technical channels, with digital sealing and AI-based fiscal fraud scoring.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated under CGI article 262(1) provided the exporter proves dispatch/transport out of France to a third-country destination. Intra-Community supplies to an EU VAT-registered customer are zero-rated under article 262-1. Services (including construction and infrastructure engineering services) are zero-rated when the place of supply is outside France under the place-of-supply rules in articles 258 to 259-0 (e.g., services relating to immovable property located in a foreign country). For construction works on a bridge physically located in France, French VAT at 20% applies; zero-rating is restricted to the professional export documentation proving overseas delivery or the foreign place of supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French tax law requires exporters to retain full supporting evidence for six years. Fraudulent or unfounded zero-rating claims are reclassified as domestic taxable supplies with VAT assessed at 20%, plus late payment interest (intérêt de retard) at 0.0024% per month and penalties: 10% for mere filing errors, 40% for intentional misstatement (manquement délibéré), and 80% in cases of abus de droit/fraud. Criminal fines under CGI article 1741 may reach EUR 500,000 with imprisonment. Retrospective clawback can cover a full six-year statutory limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as national central bank, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign exchange policy and monitoring delegated to the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) and the French Customs and Indirect Taxation Administration (DGDDI) for balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France for both current and capital account transactions, subject to EU-level free-movement of capital provisions. France maintains no general exchange-control authorisation for ordinary commercial trade, investment, or profit remittance. Capital account transfers, including direct capital injections, debt financing, and intra-group swings, are unrestricted for OECD/EU counterparties but must be reported to Banque de France for statistical and national-security screening under French Decree No. 2020-1675 (foreign investment in sensitive sectors). Profit remittance and dividend distribution in euros or foreign currency are unrestricted; however, dividends paid to non-residents are subject to French withholding tax at the statutory 25% rate unless reduced by an applicable double tax treaty, and repatriation may require an attestation of ownership and tax residency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any mandatory sale, conversion, or surrender of export proceeds into euros. Exporters are permitted to retain foreign currency in designated accounts with authorised banks. All cross-border transfers exceeding EUR 12,500 must be declared to the DGDDI/Banque de France via the monthly or quarterly balance-of-payments reporting regime, including the underlying export contract reference and currency conversion details. For public-works export contracts, no specific conversion ratio is mandated; however, foreign currency receipts used to settle external subcontractors may be netted provided full transaction documentation is maintained.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. French-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) and pan-EU payment institutions are generally unable to provide the full treasury infrastructure required for an infrastructure EPC contractor, including documentary letter of credit issuance, standby credit lines, or the IBAN-level multi-currency trust structures demanded by sovereign bond-holding employers. Legal constraints include the prohibition on EMI taking deposits or granting credit in France under the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF), and the requirement for EMI flows to sit on a licensed credit institution's balance sheet; thus, an EMI account cannot serve as the primary escrow or clearing vehicle for high-value bridge EPC payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a SARL whose ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) are non-resident legal entities, French banks mandate a face-to-face interview with the natural-person gérants (registered managers) at the bank's French head office or an ACPR-approved video-identification station. Remote onboarding is permitted only for managers residing in the EU/EEA or in territories with mutual-recognition KYC arrangements; a non-EEA resident manager must physically attend at least the initial signing and verification of corporate documents. A notarised copy of the articles of association and an original KBIS registry excerpt are mandatory. The final signatory does not have to be a French tax resident, but the SARL must maintain a registered office in France and a local day-to-day administrative presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO seated in a high-risk third country under FATF or OCC-Central Bank publications, with no local physical office in France
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO passport/travel document, corporate registry extract apostilled, notarised legal-entity structure chart, source-of-wealth declaration with audited financial statements, bank reference of the immediate parent, two letters of recommendation from EU correspondent banks, and a notarised manager mandate confirming economic purpose in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Upfront capital contribution to the capital escrow account exceeding EUR 200,000, attributed to a capital increase of an EPC contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original certified copy of the shareholders' capital increase resolution, bank crediting advices of the source funds, a Spanish/French notarial deed (as applicable), unrealised contract vs clearing study, three-way invoice of works financed, and auditors' confirmation of the SARL's balance-sheet asset backing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound SWIFT flows from sovereign treasuries or ministries of non-OECD countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed state procurement contract in the local language plus a certified English translation, official publication notice of the tender (Official Journal / state gazette), the Ministry of Finance payment certificate, bill-of-lading and progress milestone certificates, and documentary evidence that the counterparty's financial institution is not blocked by EU/UN sanctions regimes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction turnover without a full-time local CFO or in-house treasury function
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engagement letter of a European certified public accountant, independent tax advisory agreement, treasury management policy signed by the SARL gérant, list of all known subcontractors and advisers, and monthly pro-rata cash-flow projections for the first three years supported by the infrastructure contract's payment schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intra-company advance provided in a non-Euro currency (USD/GBP/CHF) via a group treasury entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group treasury policy, intercompany loan agreement with arm's length interest rate and repayment schedule, interest transfer pricing documentation under French TP rules, validated source-of-funds statement of the group entity, and foreign-currency valuation report by the lending bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use an explicit SWIFT MT103 from the parent or group treasury to the SARL's French operational account in euro. The field 20 (transaction reference) must identify the French court-approved capital increase and the field 50F must list the remitting entity that carried out the funding. The payment underlying purpose code used in the BOP declaration to Banque de France must be 'CAPTERN' (capital transfer) or 'ITR' (intercompany investment) as applicable, and the beneficiary account must be a dedicated Capital Escrow Account or corporate current account with the IBAN under FR. If funds are wired from a non-EU bank, an MT202 COVER may also be required for the agent bank. The SARL must retain: (i) the notarised deed of contribution, (ii) the resolution of the general meeting approving the capital increase, and (iii) a certificate of non-distribution (absence of any repayment of the contribution back to the remitter within 60 days) to satisfy French bank settlement finality and insolvency claw-back rules under Article L170-1 of the CMF.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT) for general subcontractor and supplier payments only after receiving a fully verified credit-screening report of the payee; (b) irrevocable, confirmed Documentary Letter of Credit (LC) under UCP600 for sovereign-backed progress milestones, with CIB bank as issuing or confirming bank to eliminate country risk; (c) an MT760 standby LC (First Demand Guarantee) for bid bonds, advanced payment guarantees and performance guarantees to the French multilaterals; and (d) direct SEPA EUR CT to EU subcontractors that have valid intracommunity VAT numbers. For all outbound flows, the SWIFT field 72 must state the reference to the host-state infrastructure agreement and the specific milestone certificate; the bank must perform an OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening on every downstream payee.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Wu-West FX Forward (Ordre de change à terme, EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/JPY) available for up to 18 months from authorised French ADB (Authorised Credit Institution) banks
Cross-Currency Swap (EUR/USD fixing with a contractual leg in USD) for the remaining three-year hedging horizon of the bridge EPC contract
European-Style FX Option (call on USD, put on EUR) limited to the net monthly disbursement requirement, not exceeding the outstanding principal exposure
FX forward with fuse-structure (FolioUpdate) allowing late extension only upon a confirmed Change Order from the Ministry of Finance
Term deposit in USD inside the SARL's foreign-currency account as a cash collateral substitute pending conversion to EUR for subcontract swings

No EUR NDF (non-deliverable forward) is permitted for EUR because the euro is freely deliverable in the EUR/USD market and the NDF market does not exist among French ADBs. Any NDF-style arrangement would be treated as an unregulated gaming transaction under Article L327-1 of the Code Monétaire et Financier and prohibited for a merchant-settlement company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual financial statements filing with the RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filing is due by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal reminder and a penalty of up to EUR 3,000 imposed on the managing director; persistent non-filing can lead to an order for compulsory closure of accounts and ultimately to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration annuelle de résultats et liasse fiscale (annual corporate income tax return for SARL assessing Impôt sur les Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) via electronic filing (REI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, deadline is the 2nd working day after 1 May of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an immediate 10% penalty on the tax due plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; after formal notice, penalty escalates to 40% if filed within 30 days or 80% if not

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation annuelle de l'exactitude des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE annual beneficial-owner confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, maintained by the Greffe de la juridiction commerciale
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, simultaneously with the deposit of financial statements; variations in shareholding must also be reported within 30 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declaration may be punished with up to EUR 30,000 fine and 6 months imprisonment for the legal representative; additional administrative fines of up to EUR 15,000 may be applied

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) annual local property-tax declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on 15 December each year for taxes above EUR 3,000; if below, payment is made on the other permissible schedule per the local tax notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or late return leads to a 10% automatic late-filing penalty; unpaid amounts trigger 10% surcharge plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SARL is subject to mandatory statutory independent audit when two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: (i) total balance sheet greater than EUR 6,000,000, (ii) net turnover greater than EUR 12,000,000, (iii) average number of employees greater than 50; given the size of an ISIC 4210 highway/bridge contractor, audit is presumed mandatory
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC 2014-03), codified in the Plan Comptable Général; IFRS is available only for consolidated accounts or regulated issuers

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For an SARL, every direct or indirect owner of more than 25% of capital or voting rights must be listed in the RBE. The legal representative must confirm the exactness of the RBE data at least annually at the same time as the filing of financial statements, and within 30 days of any beneficial-owner or stake transfer event
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Corporate Minutes (Registre de présences et PV de décisions)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 8,000-25,000 (approximately USD 8,700-27,200) for an infrastructure EPC contractor requiring a familiarised audit team

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% standard Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) rate for fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2022; reduced 15.0% rate applies to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for small enterprises meeting the turnover ceiling of EUR 10 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A 3.3% social contribution surcharge (contribution sociale sur l'IS) is levied when the aggregate IS liability exceeds EUR 763,000, yielding an effective marginal rate of 25.825% for large infrastructure contractors. Preferential regimes include: (i) the Recherche Crédit d'Impôt (CIR) at up to 30% of eligible R&D expenditures; (ii) a reduced 2.4% rate on long-term capital gains from the sale of eligible participations under the régime des plus-values de cession de titres; (iii) the carry-back of tax losses to the prior fiscal year up to EUR 1,000,000; and (iv) accelerated depreciation allowances for machinery used in heavy construction and transport infrastructure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) and annexes 2050-SD to 2059-SD, filed electronically through the EFI (Échange de Données Informatisé) portal on impots.gouv.fr via the Mode EFI professional portal or the EDI partner channel; mandatory for all SARLs subject to IS regardless of turnover.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; preliminary corporate tax installments are payable quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with final settlement upon filing the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 2065-SD and the full statutory financial statements must be filed within 3 months of the fiscal year-end (Article 223-1 of the CGI). For a calendar year-end SARL (31 December), the electronic filing deadline is 15 May of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is the 3rd month following the closing date. Paper filings, where exceptionally authorized, are due by 3 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, SIREN/SIRET number, registered office address, APE/NAF code (4210Z for highway and bridge construction), and the tax identification number of the French fiscal representative if the SARL is foreign-managed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) when the SARL has no established French management seat; provide a copy of the mandate and the representative's French tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax regime indicator confirming the entity is in the régime de l'impôt sur les sociétés, including the option for the 15% small-enterprise reduced rate and the 25% standard rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the application of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the applicable Double Tax Treaty if the SARL is held by a non-resident parent; indicate the shareholding percentage and holding period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover (Article 209 CGI) including all infrastructure EPC contract revenue recognized under the percentage-of-completion method (avancement), grossing up project milestones, variation orders, and retention amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide turnover attributable to the French permanent establishment or the French SARL as a separate taxable entity; exclude intra-group dividends, exempt capital gains on qualified participations, and recycled VAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal taxable income after reconciliation of statutory accounting profit with tax adjustments: depreciation, provisions, non-deductible fines, tax-exempt subsidies, carried-forward deficits, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the add-back of the 3.3% social contribution if the IS base exceeds the EUR 763,000 threshold; deduct the allocable share of financing costs subject to the earnings-stripping limitation rules (Article 212 bis CGI).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of tax losses carried forward from prior fiscal years; French law limits carryforward to a 5-year window with an additional EUR 1,000,000 annual cap on the excess over the capped fraction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French SARL wholly owned by a non-resident, loss utilization remains available subject to the anti-abuse demonstration of business substance; ERP loss usage cannot be transferred to the French entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits available against IS: CIR (research credit), apprenticeship tax credit, competitiveness employment credit (if still applicable), and foreign tax credits from source jurisdictions on foreign project revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned SARL may claim foreign tax credits only to the extent the underlying profits were earned through a French taxable permanent establishment; attach waiver certificates for credit claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net corporate income tax liability after applying the 15% reduced rate and the 25% standard rate, the 3.3% social surcharge, and deducting quarterly advance payments and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the quarterly advance payments (tiers provisionnels) were made by the 15th of March/June/September/December; final balance due is payable no later than the 15 May filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase of the net tax due if the return is filed late but tax is paid on time; 40% increase if the tax is paid late; 80% increase in cases of fraudulent maneuvers or organized concealment. A formal notice (mise en demeure) that remains unanswered for 30 days escalates the penalty from 10% to 40%. Late payment interest (intérêt de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum) from the statutory due date. Failure to file is a criminal offense under Article 1741 CGI, punishable by up to EUR 500,000 in fines and imprisonment for directors who intentionally conceal activity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25.0% statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders under Article 119 bis-2 CGI; reduced to 0% when the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies (minimum 10% direct shareholding held at least 2 years) and to treaty rates of 0% to 15% for residents of treaty jurisdictions; a 12.8% flat tax (PFU) applies to dividends distributed to non-resident individuals, plus 17.2% social levies unless waived under treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC / formulaire 5000 or equivalent) from its jurisdiction, (ii) provide to the French paying agent a completed Form 5002 (attestation de domicile) and, where required, Form 5003 demonstrating economic entitlement and absence of abusive conduit structures, (iii) demonstrate the minimum holding period (typically 2 years) and minimum shareholding (typically 10%) required by the applicable DTA and the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and (iv) if tax was over-withheld at the 25% statutory rate, file a refund claim (réclamation contentieuse) with the local tax authority (SIE) under Article L.190 of the Book of Tax Procedures by 31 December of the second year following the year of distribution. The French tax administration may request an expert opinion on the beneficial ownership of the dividend and an anti-abuse review under the Principal Purpose Test of the MLI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 30.0% statutory withholding tax on patent royalties, know-how fees, and other intellectual property payments to non-residents (Article 125 A CGI); exemption applies under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive when a 25% direct shareholding is held for at least 2 years; treaty reductions typically range from 0% to 10%. Interest: 0% statutory withholding tax on ordinary debt interest paid by a French SARL to non-resident lenders (France does not levy a domestic WHT on arm's-length interest); the 30% WHT is restored for interest paid to entities located in non-cooperative States (ETNC) and for excessive interest treated as constructive dividends; treaty floors of 0% to 10% apply under DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File (documentation pénalement exigible) under Article L.13 AA of the Book of Tax Procedures when the French entity's annual turnover or total assets exceed EUR 400 million. A simplified transfer pricing annex (Form 2257-SD) is mandatory when the annual turnover exceeds EUR 50 million. Country-by-Country reporting (déclaration pays par pays, Form 2258-SD) applies to French groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Infrastructure EPC contractors below the EUR 400 million threshold must still maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing evidence if they conclude cross-border intragroup transactions (management fees, guarantees, equipment leasing, engineering services).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute as in the UAE, but enforces a substantive economic substance doctrine through: (i) the judicial concept of abus de droit (Article L.64 of the Book of Tax Procedures), under which a SARL that is artificially interposed without genuine commercial, industrial, or management substance is disregarded and reattributed to its beneficial owner; (ii) the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) of Article 209 CGI for artificial chains of transactions; (iii) the OECD/G20 Principal Purpose Test incorporated into French DTAs and the MLI; and (iv) the EU ATAD anti-hybrid and controlled-foreign-company rules. For an infrastructure EPC contractor, substance is demonstrated by local staff, engineering and project-management premises, contract negotiation authority, risk assumption, and a physical bank account receiving sovereign letter-of-credit proceeds. Absence of these indicia exposes the SARL to reclassification as a shell and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of taxable profits by omitting Highway Bridge EPC contract revenue from the Form 2065 return, issuance of false invoices, use of undisclosed offshore bank accounts, or deliberate under-reporting of progress billings under the percentage-of-completion method.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI: imprisonment up to 5 years, a fine up to EUR 500,000 (doubled to EUR 1,000,000 when aggravated), and the automatic 80% penalty increase of the evaded tax plus late interest at 0.20% per month; corporate entities incur the criminal fine multiplied by a factor of 5 (EUR 2,500,000). The court may order the publication of the sanction in official media and a ban on receiving public procurement contracts for up to 5 years — fatal for an infrastructure contractor relying on sovereign tenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (managing director) is criminally liable as the author of the offense and may be personally fined and imprisoned; the tax authority may seek, under Article L.266 of the Book of Tax Procedures, joint and several civil liability of the director for the corporate tax debt when the fraud results from serious misconduct (agissements frauduleux); civil courts may order material seizure (saisie pénale) of personal assets, an exit/ travel ban (interdiction de quitter le territoire), and a 10-year prohibition on managing a commercial company (Article L.653-8 of the Commercial Code).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Omission of Tax Return (Défaut et Retard de Déclaration)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 2065-SD and annexes within the 3-month statutory deadline; omission of the balance sheet (bilan), profit and loss account, and the supplementary statement of cash flows for the bridge construction entity; refusal to respond to a mise en demeure within 30 days.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic 10% tax increase when the return is filed late with tax paid on time; 40% increase when the tax is also unpaid; 80% increase for fraudulent maneuvers; monthly late interest of 0.20%; the tax authority additionally proceeds to an automatic re-assessment (taxation d'office) and rejects the carryforward of prior-year losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be held personally liable for the full corporate tax debt if the failure to file is coupled with irregularities rendering the corporation unable to pay (insuffisance d'actif) — Article L.651-2 of the Commercial Code; bank account freezes, travel restrictions, and a personal fine of up to EUR 15,000 can be imposed for persistent non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Improper shifting of profits from the French SARL to a related foreign contractor or special-purpose vehicle through inflated equipment rental, construction management fees, interest payments, or underpriced intragroup bridge-engineering services that breach the arm's length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 57 CGI, the tax authority reallocates the shifted profits to the French entity and reassesses the IS, the 3.3% social surcharge, and corresponding VAT; a 5% annual penalty on the reallocated profit applies when no acceptable documentation is produced; if the manipulation is deemed abusive, the 80% penalty increase and Article 1741 criminal sanctions may be triggered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the intragroup contracts consolidating unadjusted transfer prices risk personal civil liability under Article L.223-22 of the Commercial Code for damages, joint liability for the reassessed tax if the structure was artificial, and criminal prosecution in cases of fictitious services; the French anti-fraud unit (DNEF) may reference the director to the public prosecutor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the French SARL as a facade entity with no local management, personnel, engineering capacity, or bank operations, while the highway and bridge construction business is de facto conducted by the non-resident parent; routing sovereign letter-of-credit proceeds through the SARL without any operational realization in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may invoke abus de droit (Article L.64 LPF) and disregard the legal fiction: the SARL's profits are reattributed to the non-resident beneficiary, exposing the shareholder to a 80% penalty on the concealed tax (in the case of an exclusively fiscal purpose) and a personal administrative fine of EUR 10,000 to EUR 20,000; treaty benefits are denied under the Principal Purpose Test; the entity is struck off the commercial register (radiation) and its bank accounts are closed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominal director of an empty shell SARL incurs personal liability for the unpaid corporate tax under Article L.266 LPF, criminal exposure for abuse of company assets (abus de biens sociaux) under Article L.241-3 of the Commercial Code with imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of EUR 375,000, a travel ban, and a commercial management ban; the court may order the piercing of the corporate veil and attachment of the director's personal and foreign assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Payment Integrity Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of the SARL's infrastructure payment rails — sovereign letters of credit and SWIFT wires — in a non-compliant manner: receipt of proceeds into undisclosed foreign accounts, unjustified rapid layering of funds to shell subcontractors in high-risk jurisdictions, use of unlicensed money transmitters, or failure to verify a sanctioned counterparty on bridge steel or cement imports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code (L.561 et seq.), the SARL faces an administrative fine up to EUR 5,000,000 and a temporary suspension of its activity; financial intermediaries may be ordered to terminate banking relations; criminal penalties for laundering of aggravated tax fraud carry up to 10 years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 in fines for natural persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is the designated AML compliance officer of the SARL and is personally liable for failing to establish a transaction monitoring framework; sanctions include a personal fine up to EUR 375,000, a permanent ban from directing a company, confiscation of proceeds, an exit ban, and extradition exposure where foreign bank accounts were used; mandatory reporting of suspicious transactions to Tracfin is a non-delegable personal duty of the director.
